reason: Cooling the lava and rock seems like a direct way to make the surface able to retain liquid water.
expectation: I expect heat to escape from the surface, leaving cooler rock, though further cooling may be needed.

alternatives.reason: Cooler air might form rain, but I want to address surface cooling first.

effect: The cooler rock can retain liquid water, so the remaining goal is to make rain.
reaction: The contrast between neighboring cool rock and hot lava makes the uneven cooling clear.
reason: Cool air above the surface seems likely to condense atmospheric water into clouds and rain.
expectation: I expect water vapor to condense, perhaps forming clouds before rain reaches the ground.

alternatives.reason: Atmospheric heat loss might also help cooling, but cooler air seems more directly related to condensation.

effect: Condensation produced clouds; gravity may now bring their water down as rain.
reaction: The distinction between clouds and a surface that can hold water is clear.
reason: Gravity acting on cloud droplets seems the direct next step toward rain reaching the ground.
expectation: I expect droplets to fall as rain, though they may need to grow first.

alternatives.reason: Further atmospheric cooling might help, but the clouds are already available.

effect: Rain is falling, but hot air and lava can return some of it to vapor before it collects.
reaction: The evaporation makes the distinction between falling rain and retained water clearer.
reason: The offered rain-and-lava combination may show how water cycles back from the hot surface and advance the rain goal.
expectation: I expect rain hitting the hot lava to boil into vapor, though it may reveal another step toward rain reaching cooler ground.

alternatives.reason: Cooling the atmosphere could also help, but I want to see what happens to the falling rain.

effect: Rain on hot lava returns to the atmosphere as steam, while neighboring cool rock can retain water.
reaction: The contrasting outcomes on nearby patches make the water cycle concrete.
reason: This is the only offered combination; atmospheric heat loss may help rain reach the ground.
expectation: I expect the atmosphere to cool as infrared energy escapes, though I am unsure what this will produce.

effect: The atmosphere cools slowly as energy escapes from its upper layers, coupling its cooling to the surface.
reaction: The distinction between impeded and stopped heat loss is useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may let the recycled steam condense again.
expectation: I expect the steam to cool and rejoin the rain cycle, though I am unsure whether rain will reach the ground.

effect: The steam has rejoined a cycle of evaporation and condensation, rather than immediately forming an ocean.
reaction: Recycling the same water makes the repeated phase changes clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination; cooler air may condense the recycled water again.
expectation: I expect renewed condensation and perhaps rain that can reach the ground, though another step may be needed.

effect: Cooling now lets more rain survive its descent; the cool rock may retain it.
reaction: The model-dependent duration of early rainfall is a useful qualification.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and cool rock should allow the rain to collect.
expectation: I expect liquid water to gather on the cool rock, though I do not know whether it will form a lasting body of water yet.

effect: Rain now stays liquid on cool rock and can accumulate in low ground; both chapter goals are complete.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the earlier surface cooling finally allow water to collect.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making rain boil back into steam showed why rain alone does not guarantee a lasting body of water, especially beside cooler rock.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sequence of recycled water and renewed condensation felt somewhat repetitive, even though it clarified the cycle.

surprise.text: The atmosphere could impede heat loss while still losing energy from its upper layers, coupling its cooling to the surface.

arbitrary.text: The later sequence was guided by single available combinations; their general purpose was clear, but I could not always predict what each would produce.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested in seeing how the retained water accumulates, though I would hope for more meaningful choices than the final single-option sequence.
